contributions.text: 2. What steps she is taking to introduce a Ukrainian GCSE.
contributions.name: Joe Powell

contributions.text: 20. What progress her Department has made on introducing a Ukrainian GCSE.
contributions.name: Richard Baker

contributions.who: The Minister for School Standards (Georgia Gould)
contributions.text: The UK Government remain steadfast in our support for Ukraine. We are proud to be delivering a GCSE in Ukrainian and intend to work with AQA to introduce the qualification, with first teaching planned for September 2028 and assessments from summer 2029. The new qualification demonstrates our solidarity with Ukraine and our wish to help young Ukrainians maintain their language and cultural heritage while supporting future work, study and engagement with Ukraine.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould

contributions.text: May I just say a huge thank you to the Minister and the team for this incredibly important announcement? I have been inundated with messages from quite emotional and delighted parents, including parents whose children were being offered GCSEs in Russian, which was completely inappropriate. Will she join me in congratulating all the teachers of Ukrainian, including those at St Mary’s trust, for their work to get us this far, and does she agree that while many of us might have learned “Slava Ukraini” in recent years, there will be more opportunities for people who want to live and work in Ukraine and support Ukraine in the future?
contributions.name: Joe Powell

contributions.text: I thank my hon. Friend for his advocacy on this important issue. We visited St Mary’s together recently and saw how much it meant to the teachers and young people who will get the chance to study this GCSE. The hard work that they are putting into maintaining this link to Ukraine will be recognised. As he says, it is an opportunity for Ukrainian young people, but there will also be the opportunity for all young people to access this qualification as we build and continue to deepen our deep ties with Ukraine.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould

contributions.text: I am a member of the Council of Europe’s network on the situation of the children of Ukraine, which has also stressed the importance of language qualifications in Ukrainian for young Ukrainians in other European countries. Will my hon. Friend agree to share learning on the introduction of this qualification in English schools with her Scottish counterpart, given that I understand that the equivalent qualification is not yet available in Scotland, where we have welcomed so many Ukrainians to our communities following the Russian invasion?
contributions.name: Richard Baker

contributions.text: We welcome the interest in the Ukrainian GCSE. We would be delighted to work with the Scottish Government and any other Governments who are interested in taking forward our approach. We think it is critically important, and we heard how much it meant to young people who have come here from Ukraine.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould

contributions.text: Further to the point from the hon. Member for Glenrothes and Mid Fife (Richard Baker), the news of the Ukrainian GCSE has been welcomed in Edinburgh, where they are already running weekend classes at the community centre to keep young Ukrainians in this country in touch with their heritage and culture should they want to return after the war. As well as talking to the Scottish Government, is the Minister willing to talk to those community groups about how young people can be encouraged to take up the GCSE through the schools that will offer that qualification?
contributions.name: Christine Jardine

contributions.text: I would be delighted to talk to those community groups. When we spoke to St Mary’s school, they told us that they run a network of supplementary schools and they assured us that those conversations are already happening with schools in Scotland and around England. We would like to work with them to ensure that any young person who wants to access this qualification can do so.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould

contributions.text: I thank the Minister for her helpful and comprehensive answers. In my constituency we have large numbers of Ukrainian children in schools, for instance in Ballynahinch high school and Movilla, Regent House and Glastry schools. Can the Minister share the strategy and policy for the Ukrainian GCSE that the Government are bringing forward in England with the relevant Northern Ireland Minister, so that we could do the same in Northern Ireland?
contributions.name: Jim Shannon

contributions.text: As well as speaking to the Scottish Government, I would be delighted to talk to the Northern Irish Government about the new GCSE—I have a busy week ahead of me with those conversations.
contributions.name: Georgia Gould
